analysis.evidence: אֶת־הַיּוֹנָה marks the dove as the object, and מֵאִתּוֹ means “from him.” Noah sent the dove out to see whether the floodwaters had receded.
analysis.morphology: Piel wayyiqtol, third-person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ and no suffix

analysis.evidence: In וַיְשַׁלַּח אֶת הַיּוֹנָה, “he sent out the dove,” אֶת marks הַיּוֹנָה, “the dove,” as the definite direct object of וַיְשַׁלַּח.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֶת marks הַיּוֹנָה as the direct object of וַיְשַׁלַּח. Noah sends the dove out to see whether the water has receded from the ground.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute common noun with prefixed definite article הַ־.

analysis.evidence: Noah sends the dove לִרְאוֹת, and the following question הֲקַלּוּ הַמַּיִם specifies what he wants to learn: whether the waters have receded from the ground.
analysis.morphology: Qal infinitive construct with prefixed לִ־ expressing purpose

analysis.evidence: After לִרְאוֹת ‘to see’, הֲ־ introduces an indirect question. The plural verb agrees with הַמַּיִם ‘the waters’, and מֵעַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה ‘from the surface of the ground’ shows what Noah wanted to learn by sending the dove.
analysis.morphology: Interrogative הֲ־ + Qal perfect, third person common plural.

analysis.evidence: In הֲקַלּוּ הַמַּיִם מֵעַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה, Noah asks whether the waters have receded from the surface of the ground. עַל locates the waters upon that surface, and מֵ־ marks movement away from it.
analysis.morphology: Preposition עַל with prefixed מִן in the form מֵ־.

analysis.evidence: פְּנֵי is in construct with הָאֲדָמָה, forming “the surface of the ground.” Noah sends the dove to see whether the waters have receded from that surface.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, common gender, plural construct, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In מֵעַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה, “from the surface of the ground,” פְּנֵי is in construct with הָאֲדָמָה. Noah sends the dove to see whether the waters have receded from that surface.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute noun with prefixed definite article הָ־.
analysis.sense: the ground underfoot; the face of the earth
